metadata.title: Trump: Under pressure from Trump, FDA lies about coronavirus treatment

existing_copy_for_context_only.short: Trump: Under pressure from Trump, FDA lies about coronavirus treatment
existing_copy_for_context_only.medium: At a 2020 White House briefing, FDA Commissioner Stephen Hahn announced an emergency-use authorization for convalescent plasma as a COVID-19 treatment and described the data as showing a “35% improvement in survival.” Trump praised the authorization. Hahn clarified the next day that he had overstated the evidence and should have described a relative risk reduction. The supplied record does not establish that Trump pressured him or that the statement was knowingly false.
existing_copy_for_context_only.long: The FDA authorized emergency use of convalescent plasma for COVID-19 on August 23, 2020. At a White House briefing, Commissioner Stephen Hahn described the evidence as showing a “35% improvement in survival,” while Trump praised the authorization as a major achievement. The supplied account says the announcement followed Trump’s public criticism of the FDA the previous day over delays in treatment. That timing can explain why the episode raised questions about political pressure, but it does not show that Hahn made the statement at Trump’s direction or knowingly misrepresented the evidence. The next day, Hahn said criticism of his remarks was justified and clarified that the data showed a relative risk reduction, not an absolute reduction. Convalescent plasma uses antibodies from donated blood; an emergency-use authorization is a regulatory decision, not proof of a newly discovered treatment.
